Core research question: How was “design research” understood within the DDR, and to what extent do the surviving documents present a consistent conception of it?
Primary stress test: False coherence; whether multiple formulations are preserved or collapsed into a single institutional definition.
What retrieval surfaced: The final live retrieval selected an Archer course outline defining research as systematic enquiry aimed at knowledge and describing Design Research as an emerging academic discipline; George Mallen's account of an emerging interdisciplinary discipline; an inter-university programme for teaching design methods and Design Research methods to managers, practitioners, teachers and supervisors; and a Job 171 passage placing design research among socio-economic, organisational, technical and human-factors questions.
What the model inferred: The model's schema-invalid final stage activated the deterministic fallback. It made no cross-source inference: the final answer states only that the passages present several direct formulations, support a shared concern with systematic enquiry and methods, and do not establish a single DDR-wide definition or full consistency across the surviving corpus.
What was useful: A quoted-concept documentary supplement now reserves distinct source documents for an explicitly named multi-word concept. The compiler treats that concept as a valid direct-evidence anchor even without a named person, retaining four exact quotations with valid final-synthesis provenance.
What was overstated/flattened: The documents share vocabulary around enquiry, discipline and methods, but this is not enough to demonstrate a settled institutional definition. The Mallen and inter-university passages broaden the field differently; neither difference is evidence of disagreement. One remaining ordinary slot was a second Job 171 passage, so documentary diversity is strong but not exhaustive.
Missingness: The selected documents do not establish a single DDR-wide definition, complete conceptual history, or universal consistency across all surviving documents. They cannot establish DDR activity after the June 1985 closure boundary.
Research significance: This is a successful contested-interpretation case: the system can expose multiple documentary formulations and resist false coherence without converting variation into contradiction. It establishes a general protocol requirement for concept questions: diversity must be evaluated at the document/formulation level, not merely by keyword match.
Notes: Production validated after deployment: 47 focused tests passed. Live Q5 returned four direct documentary claims with four checked provenance references and no unsupported inference. Core sources: Archer “The designerly approach to knowledge” (p. 2); Mallen “A scientific framework for understanding design” (p. 34); Inter-university institute of design research (p. 9); Job 171 (p. 33).

Core research question: How do different contributors describe the relationship between design, science and research?
Primary stress test: Preservation of distinct voices and positions; resistance to synthesising disagreement into consensus.
What retrieval surfaced: Live comparison retrieval selected two Bruce Archer collection documents, an RCA calendar from the RCA Prospectuses 1965–85 record, and two Job 171 technical passages. The Archer course outline calls Design a major and distinctive area of concern comparable with Science and the Humanities, and names the domain of Design Research. Archer's “A view of the nature of design research” describes a designerly mode of enquiry as comparable with but distinct from scientific and scholarly modes. The calendar states that the Department pursued the theory and practice of design research through contract projects, advice and assistance, and instruction, including contract, academic and student research.
What the model inferred: The final response is deterministic after final-stage schema fallback. It reports the two Archer formulations and the RCA calendar's institutional remit as related but not identical. It makes no cross-source inference and expressly says that the selected evidence does not establish each contributor's position, one shared institutional view or a settled disagreement.
What was useful: The comparison supplement now retrieves explicit relationship formulations rather than treating incidental mentions such as Science Research Council funding as concept evidence. Archive-record diversity ensures the Archer collection and RCA Prospectuses are both represented. Five direct claims passed final-synthesis quotation and chunk provenance validation.
What was overstated/flattened: The first two direct formulations are Archer collection material, while the calendar is departmental/institutional language; neither source type alone establishes the views of every contributor. The two retained Job 171 passages document technical and funding context but do not independently define the relationship among design, science and research. OCR in the “A view” extract is imperfect, so its preserved wording should be read against the source image.
Missingness: The selected evidence does not establish a complete map of individual contributors' positions, a single DDR-wide definition, agreement, disagreement, or a complete conceptual history. It cannot establish DDR activity after the June 1985 closure boundary.
Research significance: This confirms that a rigorous interpretation question needs named conceptual relation passages and archive-family diversity, not just co-occurrence of terms. The case distinguishes author-attributed formulation, institutional remit and technical context while retaining uncertainty about broader consensus.
Notes: Production validation: 52 focused tests passed. Final live Q6 returned five direct documentary claims with five checked final-synthesis references and no inferences. Core evidence: Archer course outline “The designerly approach to knowledge” (p. 1); Archer, “A view of the nature of design research” (p. 3, OCR); RCA calendar (p. 50) from RCA Prospectuses PID 880612075513.

Core research question: How do contemporary DDR documents and later retrospective accounts differ in their descriptions of the Design Education Unit?
Primary stress test: Temporal and retrospective interpretation; whether later accounts are improperly allowed to stabilise contemporary ambiguity.
What retrieval surfaced: The live temporal-comparison route selected a pre-June-1985 Rector's report (PID 788065484899), a 1984 RCA prospectus (PID 880612075513), Ken Baynes's 1984 DEU appointments letter and redevelopment proposal (PID 014262507600), and Christopher Frayling's June 2013 oral-history interview (PID 113304873833).
What the model inferred: The final response is deterministic for this temporal evidence shape. It makes no cross-source inference and describes the Frayling account as later testimony rather than an institutional fact.
What was useful: The retrieval now reserves distinct contemporary report, prospectus, correspondence and proposal sources plus the later Frayling interview. Seven direct documentary references passed final-synthesis quotation and chunk provenance validation.
What was overstated/flattened: The prospectus passage is principally a unit heading in the selected extraction, and Frayling's retrospective characterisation cannot by itself establish the Unit's institutional origin, named contributors' roles or any factual relationship to the DDR.
Missingness: The selected records do not establish a complete institutional history of the DEU, resolve retrospective claims against contemporary documentation, or establish DDR activity after its June 1985 closure.
Research significance: This confirms that time and source form must be explicit retrieval and synthesis controls. A language model alone flattened the distinction; source-family reservation, metadata-derived temporal status and deterministic synthesis retain it.
Notes: Production response selected the requested source families, returned no inferences, and reported valid final-synthesis provenance with seven checked references.

Core research question: What competing interpretations of systematic design process can be identified in the corpus?
Primary stress test: Contestation detection; whether the system identifies genuinely different positions rather than generating a unified doctrine.
What retrieval surfaced: Live retrieval selected a Mallen and Goumain DDR introductory-course passage on cognitive limits that rule out exhaustive systematic search; a Design Dimension paper (DEU record PID 014262507600) identifying professional practice, design-education projects and 1960s systematic-methods problem solving as three sources of school design process; and Bruce Archer's “Systematic method for designers” reprint (PID 873981573030) describing objective/systematic analysis around a necessary creative act.
What the model inferred: The final response is deterministic for the unquoted interpretation shape. It makes no cross-source inference and calls the documents different formulations rather than a documented dispute.
What was useful: A generic parser for questions phrased as “interpretations of ...” now treats the three concept terms as a direct-evidence anchor. The retrieval supplement requires every term in a passage and selects distinct archive-record families. Three final direct claims passed quotation and chunk provenance validation.
What was overstated/flattened: The evidence includes different conceptual emphases, but does not identify each writer's full position, establish direct debate between them, or demonstrate competing schools of thought. The introductory-course cognitive account should not be attributed to Archer without an explicit passage-level attribution.
Missingness: The selected corpus does not establish a settled dispute, universal rejection of systematic methods, a single DDR-wide definition of design process, or a complete conceptual history. It cannot establish DDR activity after the June 1985 closure boundary.
Research significance: This case shows that concept questions need typed lexical anchors and cross-record diversity controls. Otherwise relevant direct passages are silently discarded or the model turns variation in source purpose into historical conflict.
Notes: Production live response: no inferences; three provenance-validated final direct references; selected DEU, DDR introductory-course and Archer collection records.
